newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T up on hopes for tobacco settlement.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T up on hopes for tobacco settlement.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc nudged to a six-month high on Monday after the company's chief executive Martin Broughton said in a television interview the company may consider a deal to settle U.S. tobacco lawsuits.
The stock was up 3-1/2p at 518-1/2 by 0929 GMT after earlier rising as high as 520p, its highest since last August.
Broughton told the BBC's Money Programme the company may be prepared to consider compensation payments as part of a general settlement package.
Yet a spokesman for B.A.T said his comments were no more than a restatement of existing company policy.
"It is no different from what we have alwayus said," said a spokesman for B.A.T., "which is that if it was in shareholders' interests then we would consider a settlement."

The spokesman said Broughton had pointed out that there was a cost in defending the large number of cases the company was now facing in the U.S., and that a settlement could be attractive "providing it was all-embracing and cast-iron."
However, he said the issue remained hypothetical because there had as yet been no approach to the tobacco industry from the various plaintiffs.
"Our message to shareholders is that if a settlement was in their interests we would consider it," he added.
Last year U.S. cigarette maker Liggett broke ranks with the rest of the industry by offering payments if plaintiffs dropped lawsuits.

Meantime shares in B.A.T, which also owns the Eagle Star insurance group, were also buoyed by continuing bid speculation in the insurance sector, with General Accident Plc up 21p at 867 and Commercial Union Plc up 20-1/2p at 757.
